walkthroughs.body_html:
Integration — a core area of A-Level Maths.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Integration brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Integration.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: What must you remember to include when finding an indefinite integral?
options: You don't need anything extra — the integral is just the antiderivative.
Definite integrals are negative only when the limits are reversed.
A constant of integration (+ C), because the derivative of any constant is zero.
You always need to add 1 to the answer to account for rounding.

mcqs.q: Can a definite integral give a negative value, even when integrating a function from left to right?
options: Yes — if the function is below the x-axis over the interval, the integral is negative.
Definite integrals are always positive because area cannot be negative.
Definite integrals are negative only when the limits are reversed.
You always need to add 1 to the answer to account for rounding.
It reaches 0 at the millionth term.
Eventually a term will be so small it equals 0.
You always need to add 1 to the answer to account for rounding.
No — it approaches 0 as the limit but no term is ever exactly 0.
